text:
ben: FYI customer reported duplicate charges after a burst — looks like our Python client retries replaying non-idempotent requests when run under forked workers (gunicorn/preload). attaching quick repro.

support-bot: Ticket #CS-8842 created for account acct-9012 :ticket: — assigned to support.

carlos: Which SDK version is the customer using?

ben: python-sdk==0.8.2 (installed via pip).

alice: Can you paste the minimal repro and the request logs?

ben: Repro (very small):
```python
# preload happens in master, then workers fork
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")

def worker():
    # non-idempotent endpoint (intentional for test)
    client.api_call("/v1/actions/run", json={"op":"charge","amount":1})

if __name__=='__main__':
    from multiprocessing import Process
    p = Process(target=worker)
    p.start()
    p.join()
```

ben: Logs from a run:
```
[2026-03-10T12:01:02Z] INFO sending request id=1 path=/v1/actions/run
[2026-03-10T12:01:02Z] INFO retrying request id=1 attempt=2 backoff=0.120s
[2026-03-10T12:01:02Z] INFO sending request id=1 path=/v1/actions/run
```
(We see two sends close together; customer saw two charges.)

alice: Do the two outgoing attempts include an Idempotency-Key header?

ben: I captured raw HTTP: first attempt has `Idempotency-Key: None` (absent), second attempt also absent. The client is supposed to auto-generate a key when none is provided.

ben: Root cause hypothesis: when master process preloads the Client, the RNG state and internal retry/jitter RNG are copied into worker on fork. The retry scheduler then produces correlated jitter across processes or fails to generate fresh idempotency keys, so retried attempts across forked processes can end up without unique keys or with identical jitter timings.

carlos: Hmm. Do we create idempotency keys via a global random.Random instance that was initialized at import time? That would be fork-unsafe.

alice: Confirmed in local run: after fork the RNG.secrets still returns the same sequence. Also saw client._default_id_key_template uses a counter that was copied. So two processes pick the same generated key (or none) and then retry behavior can replay.

devex: Short-term workaround for customers: avoid using `preload_app` with gunicorn OR explicitly call `client.reseed()` / `client.reset_idempotency_state()` in worker start hooks. Also passing an explicit `idempotency_key` from app code avoids duplicates.

ben: I pushed a small repro script and added logs to the ticket. Customer applied the workaround (generate explicit idempotency key per request) and their duplicate charges stopped.

alice: Plan: add a fork-safe init path — call os.register_at_fork to reseed RNG / reset counters in Client when available, and ensure idempotency key generation uses os.urandom-backed UUIDs instead of a global counter. I'll open a PR.

carlos: Can you add a regression test that forks and ensures two workers don't produce identical generated keys or identical backoff sequences?

alice: Yep — will include multiprocessing/fork test and a unit that monkeypatches random to ensure reseed runs.

devex: ETA on PR? We should also draft a short KB explaining the gunicorn preload caveat and the workaround.

alice: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1412 — includes os.register_at_fork re-seed, switch to uuid4 for idempotency default, and a test.

ben: Great, assigning CS ticket to eng for follow-up and letting customer know a fix is in review. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #CS-8842 updated: status -> in_progress, linked PR #1412.
